relevance_note: The paper describes seven individually labelled patients with Tangier disease ("Seven patients homozygous for Tangier disease from five unrelated kindreds were studied"), with per-patient sex, age and lipid values in Table I; no ABCA1 variant is described (1977 biochemical study).
method_note: Rows built by a short Python script from my reading; Table I row segments were copied programmatically from the Markdown and checked against the table. Patients are labelled by the initials the paper uses (Table I). Age in Table I ('Age - yr') is the age at study and is recorded as age at last evaluation. No variant table rows: the paper names no gene or variant ('homozygous for Tangier disease' is a disease statement, not a variant), so no variant rows were created and zygosity was not recorded. Families: the paper says 'five unrelated kindreds' but assigns no kindred labels; shared surname abbreviations (La., Lo.) were not used to infer families. Low HDL: each patient's HDL cholesterol (0-6 mg/dl, Table I) plus the sentence on the near total absence of HDL in the seven patients was used for 'low HDL cholesterol'. Hypertriglyceridemia: 'Four of the patients were hypertriglyceridemic' is an unnamed count; only C. No. and T. La. are named as hypertriglyceridemic; the other two were not inferred from Table I values. LDL: LDL mass (analytic ultracentrifugation, six patients, all but Pa. Lo.) was reduced in E. La., T. La., C. No. and normal in 'the other three subjects' (Pe. Lo., J. St., R. Ja.); the paper says LDL cholesterol does not reflect LDL mass, so the checklist item 'low LDL cholesterol' was left not reported; the group-level statement that LDL cholesterol was 'significantly less' than controls was not assigned to individuals. E. La.'s triglyceride rise (639 mg/dl) was diet-induced (carbohydrate feeding) and was not used for the hypertriglyceridemia checklist item. Oral contraceptive use is recorded under treatment_summary for E. La. although it is not a treatment for the disease. Study diets (unrestricted vs low-fat high-carbohydrate) are experimental conditions, not treatments, and were not recorded. Lipoprotein composition values (Tables II, III, V) and C-apoprotein percentages were not recorded as phenotypic features. Publication year is not printed (only 'Received for publication 25 May 1977 and in revised form 31 August 1977'), so year is null. Text spelling inconsistency: 'T. La' (no final period) in one sentence vs 'T. La.' in the tables; treated as the same person. Subject S. Ja. (type 3 hyperlipoproteinemia) and controls are out of scope. The Markdown has OCR damage (merged columns); no spans were joined across damaged text.
